simple.meaning: בַּרְקָן (barqân) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a thorn (perhaps as burning brightly).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 8:7. The surrounding context includes city, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בַּרְקָן (H1303) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H1303. barqanim בַּרְקָנִים noun masculine plural briers (so Vrss Ki and others, also Stu q. v., Be, v unknown; compare || קוֺצִים ; > JDMich, Thes and others threshing-sledges , furnished with sharp ( glittering ) stones) Judg 8:7 וְאֶתהַֿבּ הַמִּדְבָּר אֶתקֿוֺצֵי ׳אֶתבְּֿשַׂרְכֶם וְדַשְׁתִּ֫י (see also דושׁ ) and I will thresh your flesh together with the thorns of the wilderness and the briers ; 8:16 סֻכּוֺת אַנְשֵׁי אֵת בָּהֶם הַבּ וְאֶת הַמִּדְבָּר וְאֶתקֿוֺצֵי הָעִיר אֶתזִֿקְנֵי ׳וַיִּקַּח וַיֹּדַע (read וַיָּדָשׁ for ᵐ5 וַיֹּדַע Bu RS 114 ; compare Stu Be) and he took the thorns of the wilderness and the briers and threshed , etc.

occurrences.englishText: Gideon said, “Therefore when Yahweh has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.”
He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.
